title: Governor Newsom Signs Fusion Legislation and Allocates State Capital to Advance California Quantum Infrastructure - Quantum Computing Report
gist: California Governor Newsom announced a $30M joint quantum/deep-space allocation, signed fusion (SB 925) and advanced-nuclear (AB 2647) bills, and put a $7.5B Science and Health Research Bond on the March 2028 ballot explicitly to hedge against federal research funding fluctuations. UCLA's Quantum Innovation Hub has signed Boeing for quantum networking and space/defense communications work.

insights.claim: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced a $30 million joint budget allocation for quantum and deep-space research, expanding the Quantum California initiative to university hubs, public-private startup incubators and hardware supply-chain infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State-level quantum funding is growing but remains small relative to federal and private capital in the sector.
insights.locator: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed

insights.claim: Newsom signed SB 895 placing a $7.5 billion California Science and Health Research Bond Act on the March 2028 ballot, designed to mitigate potential federal research funding fluctuations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals states anticipate federal research cuts and are preparing to self-fund university R&D, a hedge for academic-spinout pipelines.
insights.quote: Designed to mitigate potential federal research funding fluctuations

insights.claim: California's quantum funding stack layers multiple smaller programs: a $4.0M dedicated quantum R&D grant, a $9.74M Jobs First grant to the UCLA-led SoCal Quantum Alliance, a $37.5M five-year NSF renewal for UC Berkeley's CIQC, a $2.7M Quantum FAST Challenge and a $3.0M workforce accelerator fund.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Funding is fragmented and workforce-heavy, pointing to talent bottlenecks as a key constraint for the quantum industry.

insights.claim: SB 925 directs the California Energy Commission to build a strategic plan, certification protocols and environmental review frameworks to commercialize fusion energy and scale fusion manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Regulatory scaffolding for fusion in the largest US state economy could lower permitting risk for fusion startups.
insights.locator: The legislative package includes Senate Bill 925

insights.claim: AB 2647 mandates a statewide technical assessment of integrating advanced nuclear technologies to support grid reliability toward California's 100% zero-carbon electricity target by 2045.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: California, historically nuclear-skeptical, studying advanced nuclear for firm power is a notable policy shift for SMR developers.
insights.locator: The legislative package includes Senate Bill 925

insights.claim: The UCLA Quantum Innovation Hub has secured Boeing as an industry partner for physical-layer quantum networking, fiber entanglement distribution and space/defense communications, including an on-site entanglement-swapping testbed for multi-node network modeling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Aerospace primes are positioning in quantum networking for defense communications, a nearer-term quantum revenue niche than computing.

insights.claim: California's quantum strategy ties together corporate R&D nodes (AWS Center for Quantum Computing at Caltech, Microsoft Station Q, Google Quantum AI) with local critical mineral production at MP Materials' rare earth facility to secure end-to-end hardware supply chains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Framing rare-earth supply as part of quantum strategy links MP Materials to the tech-sovereignty narrative.
